content.thinking:
I'm checking the claims about the shop slowdown: shoppers saw requests lag for the stated duration, memory filling up appears to be the cause, and Argus puts the lost takings at the estimated figure.

I'm going through the remaining claims: the figures for lost takings and the missing paging, the restart that was confirmed, and the draft fix that has not run and has changed nothing so far.

supported.quote: The io-shop online shop slowed down for some shoppers for {duration}.
rows: What a reader saw: Shop requests slowed down for shoppers

supported.quote: The shop's memory kept filling up until it slowed.
rows: Why, in plain words: The shop's memory kept filling up until the shop slowed down

supported.quote: This was most likely because the shop kept a note of every shopper who opened their account page and only cleared those notes when it was restarted.
rows: Why, in plain words: ... most likely because it kept a note of every shopper who opened their account page and only cleared those notes when it was restarted

supported.quote: Argus estimates the lost takings at {customer_loss}.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: Argus restarted io-shop, and the restart was confirmed.
Argus also proposed a fix, which is still a draft.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #542 - opened as a draft

supported.quote: It hasn't been put into use yet and has changed nothing so far.
rows: What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
The fix it proposed: PR #542 ... opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
